newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First-National coalition talks move onto policy.
newsitem.headline: NZ First-National coalition talks move onto policy.

text.p: Negotiating teams from the caretaker National Party government and New Zealand First party held three hours of coalition talks on Wednesday that for the first time dealt with policy issues.
After the meeting, Prime Minister Jim Bolger would only say the next meeting between the two parties would he held next Wednesday -- a day later than had been scheduled earlier in the day.

New Zealand First leader Winston Peters, whose party holds the balance of power after an inconclusive election 11 days ago, said the time had been changed because his team was meeting the main opposition Labour Party on Tuesday and there was a Cabinet meeting that day too.
Asked to characterise the meeting today he said: "The same way I'm sure Mr Bolger indicated to you."
Peters said if Bolger had revealed nothing he was not at liberty to say anything either.
But he said a timetable for further meetings with both parties had been set and there could be two or three meetings on some days.
"We have provided (our caucus) with a briefing and will be doing so on a regular basis," Peters said.
He said it was "a given" that the talks today had got down to policy discussions.
"We are still talking about certain protocols to be followed. I think there is no doubt that... these talks will be resolved very quickly by international comparison.
"There will be a lot of intensive work. We realise that now. How can we report on things when you haven't had a chance to talk to your fellow parties about anything?
"I am asking again for the people of this country to be patient and for the media to understand their role," Peters said. He said progress reports on the talks would be issued.

Peters said earlier on Wednesday that the New Zealand dollar's recent rise lent urgency to the coalition talks, and he believed they could be wrapped up within six weeks. Peters has repeatedly said the dollar is too high.
